The split comes from the only US dataset that measures it: 'Of the 165 patients with biopsies available for review, 159 were classified as C3G (N=98) or IC-MPGN (N=61)' (Dixon BP et al., Clin J Am Soc Nephrol 2026, doi:10.2215/CJN.0000001118, PMC13549497, 204 confirmed MPGN cases across seven US paediatric health systems in PEDSnet, 2009-2019). 98/159 = 0.6164, leaving 0.3836 of the pool as idiopathic IC-MPGN, which is what APPARENT (NCT05755386, Phase 3, 106 participants, primary completion 2028-10-27) is for
column12: the split is measured in children and the adult split is probably different: a US biopsy archive study found the most restrictive C3-only immunofluorescence definition captured only 8% of MPGN type 1 cases against half of dense deposit disease (Hou J et al., Kidney Int 2014;85(2):450-456, doi:10.1038/ki.2013.340), which points to a lower C3G share of adult MPGN and so a larger layer than this. The same PEDSnet paper also reports that 16 of 47 patients with more than one native biopsy had a mix of C3G and IC-MPGN biopsies, so the split is not even stable within a patient. Taking the paediatric figure is the conservative direction
